written.myAnswer: Market analysis helps a business understand its target customers, their needs and buying habits, the size and trends of the market, and its competitors. This information helps the business choose suitable products, prices, and strategies and reduces the risk of making poor decisions. For example, a local bakery could ask people in its area which baked goods they buy, compare prices and products at nearby bakeries, and use the findings to decide what to sell and at what price.

A revenue model explains how a business will earn income, such as what it will sell, how it will price its products or services, and what sources of revenue it will use. It is essential to a business plan because it shows how the business expects to bring in money and helps assess whether its plans can be financially sustainable.

The bookstore would first research local students’ reading habits, including the types of books they need or prefer, how often they buy books, and what prices they can afford. It would also compare competitors such as nearby bookshops and online sellers, looking at their selection, prices, and delivery services. The bookstore would earn income from selling textbooks, reference books, and other popular titles, with possible additional income from delivery charges. To promote the business, it could post book recommendations and offers on social media, use a website that students can find through search engines, and send email updates about new books and discounts.
